clue.text: The footwear of almost everyone on the beach

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: a beach is covered in sand

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: everyone means all

explanation.surface: A remark about what nearly every holidaymaker on the seashore wears on their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandal is an open shoe held on by straps, one kind of footwear.

indicators.note: without means outside, so the support goes round the cutting remark

parts.note: a sling supports an injured arm
a cutting remark is a tart one

explanation.surface: A gardener's cry on finding a plant prop with no cutting attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense outside: SLING goes round TART. 'cutting' looks like a gardener's slip but is an adjective for sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: Startling means surprising, so very unexpected that it gives a jolt.
Sharp pointed pins prick the skin, and to keep teasing someone is to irritate them.

parts.note: reads as a shopper's verdict on a product but means the flavour lingering in the mouth of one who has eaten

explanation.definitionFit: The taste that remains after eating or drinking is the lasting effect on whoever consumed it.

clue.text: Nice account given by a man of the cloth

parts.note: a curate is a clergyman, a man of the cloth

explanation.surface: A pleasant bank statement handed over by a vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' at the start looks like plain praise, but it is used in its older sense of exact or finely judged, as in 'a nice distinction'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice in its precise sense, as in a nice distinction, means exact or correct.

indicators.note: exceptionally means in an unusual way, so the letters are set in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A big bush that will not fit inside a home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exceptionally' rearranges CANTHOUSE; the apostrophe adds no letter. Ceanothus is the Californian lilac.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceanothus, the Californian lilac, is a sizeable flowering bush.

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Applied in running the 11-plus exam system.
explanation.walkthrough: The 11-plus was an exam English children sat at about eleven to decide their secondary school; the letters run across 'plus education', and 'organising' is surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Employed means put to use, made use of.

indicators.note: accepted by means taken inside, so the beer holds the assignment

parts.note: stout is a dark beer, so it stands for ale
a post is an appointment or assigned job

explanation.surface: A task taken on by a portly preacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stout' looks like an adjective for the evangelist but is a beer, ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle is a missionary who spreads the gospel, a preaching evangelist.

clue.text: A number engaged in tree-climbing for exercise

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, from bottom to top
engaged in means the number goes inside the tree

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: A figure is busy going up trees to keep fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaged in' puts X inside TREE, making TREXE, and 'climbing' reads it upwards. The printed answer EXEAT cannot come from this wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert a power or influence is to exercise it.

clue.text: A document penned in the old-fashioned way

definitions.meaning: the archaic past participle of write

explanation.definitionFit: A writ is a court order, and writ is also the old form of written, as in 'writ large'.

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
improved means made better

explanation.surface: A helper lacking something wants a piece of writing polished.
explanation.definitionFit: An abettor or abetter is one who helps or encourages another, usually in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Holding so many is a little daunting

indicators.note: holding means one piece contains the other, so the little one wraps round the others

parts.note: a wee is a little, as in a wee bit
taken as written
M, the Roman numeral for a thousand, stands for many

explanation.surface: Containing so many people is slightly intimidating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding' at the front means A WEE (a little) goes round SO and M.
explanation.definitionFit: Something awe-inspiring can be overwhelming and intimidating, hence daunting.

clue.text: Allowance made for a rotten oil distribution

indicators.note: distribution spreads the letters of these words out into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Some leeway is given for a share-out of bad oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distribution' rearranges the letters of A ROTTEN OIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Toleration means allowing or putting up with something, an allowance made for it.

parts.note: a proofreader's mark in the margin asking that a crossed-out word be restored, Latin for let it stand

explanation.definitionFit: Stet is the editor's instruction that deleted text should stand after all, a request to restore it.

parts.note: charming reads as delightful but means casting charms or spells, so the woman is a witch and this is what she flies on

explanation.definitionFit: Witches in folklore ride through the air on a besom, their vehicle.

clue.text: A flash and trendy worker set about a good man

indicators.note: set about means placed around, so the first pieces surround the good man

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy
the ant is the crossword's usual worker
ST, saint, is a good man

explanation.surface: A fashionable labourer standing round a decent fellow, all in a flash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set about' puts ST (saint, a good man) inside IN plus ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean a very short moment, as in 'in a flash' or 'in an instant'.

indicators.note: awful means badly done, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A rowdy reveller is a dreadful bully.
explanation.definitionFit: To bully someone is to intimidate them, to frighten them into submission.

clue.text: Tackle little beasts around the North, then the South

indicators.note: around means the beasts go round the next piece

parts.note: hares are small animals
N is the abbreviation for north
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Taking on small animals across the North of England and then the South.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tackle' looks like a verb about confronting, but it is the noun for gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Tackle is equipment, and the straps and gear for a draught horse are its tackle.

definitions.meaning: a frame for carrying the sick or wounded
the torture device that pulls a body longer

explanation.definitionFit: A stretcher carries patients like a litter, and the rack was an instrument that pulled limbs taut.

clue.text: Glare when a key is demanded by youngsters

parts.note: G is a musical key
a litter is a brood of young animals

explanation.surface: Children demanding a key make for a harsh light.
explanation.definitionFit: Glitter and glare are both bright, dazzling light.

definitions.meaning: having no taste left behind, from the answer to 3 down

explanation.definitionFit: Insipid food lacks flavour, and insipid talk is dull and uninspiring.

clue.text: Less kind, but showing more grit

definitions.meaning: having more small pebbles or stones in it

explanation.definitionFit: Stony describes a cold, unfeeling heart and also ground full of pebbles, so the comparative fits both.

parts.note: ex means former, previous
an act is a performance

explanation.surface: Careless during an earlier show.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone punctilious is precise, so one who is imprecise or loose with details is the opposite.
A pass is a ticket granting access, and to pass a car is to go by it on the road.

clue.text: Ropes in the rigging causing problem

indicators.note: rigging can mean arranging or setting up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lines tangled in a ship's rigging cause trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the rigging' rearranges ROPES; on a ship the rigging is its ropes, which makes the surface seamless.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is a puzzling question, a tricky problem.

clue.text: The new scent is not true to type

indicators.note: new means these letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A fragrance launch that does not suit its intended character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges SCENT IS NOT; 'The' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something consistent keeps to the same pattern, behaving as expected of its kind.

clue.text: Try to decide on cocktail making

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece on another sits below it

parts.note: to see, as in 'I'll see what to do', is to decide
the tail of the word cock, its last letter, is K

explanation.surface: Trying to settle on which mixed drink to make.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' is read as the tail of 'cock', giving K, placed after SEE.
explanation.definitionFit: To seek to do something is to attempt it.

parts.note: overweight means fat

explanation.surface: A rude remark about a heavy group of English people.
explanation.definitionFit: One's lot in life is one's destiny.

parts.note: singers of the highest voice part, who never take a bass or alto line

explanation.definitionFit: Soprani, the Italian plural of soprano, are singers of the highest vocal register.

parts.note: grave reads as solemn but means a burial place: words of praise on a headstone

explanation.definitionFit: An epitaph is the inscription on a tombstone, commonly praising the person buried there.

clue.text: Paid ransom for certain military personnel held

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
held, in the sense of judged or believed, means deemed

explanation.surface: Money was handed over to free some captured soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: To redeem a captive is to buy their freedom, paying the price demanded.

parts.note: the skate is a flat fish

explanation.surface: An athlete going fishing, is that correct?
explanation.definitionFit: A skater takes part in figure or speed skating, so is a sportsman.
